limitations: Per-tool-call token usage is unavailable: the harness records usage per session (and per model call), not per tool call, so every tokensIn/tokensOut/totalTokens field in toolCalls is null.
Temperature and any provider-side thinking budget are not recorded by the harness; only reasoning disabled, max iterations 250 and max output tokens unset are known.
Token counts are the harness's session totals for the measured session, taken from its session record (state.db sessions table).

Tool-call durations are the gap between the assistant turn that issued the call and that call's tool result, from the session's message timestamps; calls issued in parallel share a turn start, so their durations overlap.

The subagent's workspace context was supplied as its task context, but Hermes records the subagent session cwd as the parent's checkout (C:/Data/ZZZScratch/Source/Roslynk/174) rather than the condition worktree; the standard session resolved the fixture to the parent checkout's Benchmarks/TestSolution (identical content to the worktree at the same commit) and the roslynk session used absolute worktree paths. Neither session read anything outside Benchmarks/TestSolution.

Roslynk availability is harness-wide configuration: config.yaml mcp_servers.roslynk.enabled was set to false for the standard session and restored to true before the roslynk session (backup config.yaml.bench-bak-20261027T161735Z). The harness's tool registry was rebuilt for each session, so the standard session saw no Roslynk tool.

The roslynk session reached Roslynk through the harness's generic tool_call wrapper, so the session record names the calls tool_call; the tool names in toolCalls were mapped from each wrapper invocation. It also spent one call on tool_search to discover the Roslynk tool names (8012 result bytes).

Roslynk tool-call durations (0.1–0.5 s) are far below the harness's own MCP round-trip latency for a first call in a session; the recorded durations are harness timestamps, not Roslynk-internal timings.
